science_vegetable: Mitigating Isolated-Confined-Extreme (ICE) Third-Quarter cortisol cascades and autonomic hypervigilance through structured communal roast rituals and oxytocin vagal buffering.
summary: Elias uses deadpan stubbornness to halt a mutiny over Kaio's improvised soup filter, preserving the communal roast ritual before handing off to Elara.
text:
The table was silent. Not the good, tired silence of a job well done. The sharp, brittle silence of sixteen people who had been breathing the same recycled air for too long.

Elias sat at the far end of the long timber table, intending to archive the linguistic and epistemic memory of the sixteen so nothing true is lost. He monitored the Third-Quarter isolation micro-stressors across the polymaths, noting Silas tapping a frantic rhythm against a titanium plate and Jane rubbing her temples. Autonomic hypervigilance had saturated the subterranean dining hall, replacing their baseline trust with a corrosive, paranoid tension.

Ryn stood at the head of the table. She held a dripping, unidentifiable gray mass aloft with a pair of metallurgical tongs, the bioluminescent moss on the walls casting a sickly green hue over the object.

"I requested a secondary mesh screen," Ryn stated, her voice carrying the flat neutrality of an imminent detonation. "You used a sock."

"It was sterilized!" Kaio protested from across the hearth. "I boiled it in the autoclave for twenty minutes. It functions perfectly as an improvised particulate filter, Ryn. We adapt."

The fragile equilibrium shattered. Hector slammed a fist on the timber, demanding a complete overhaul of the quartermaster's sanitization protocol. Willow countered with an aggressive defense of field biology. A dozen overlapping arguments erupted over the steaming pot of stew. The entire table nearly mutinied because Kaio filtered soup stock through a sock. But the sudden acoustic assault triggered a physiological alarm within Elias, causing a sharp pressure to blossom behind his sternum.

He closed his leather-bound journal, pressing his palms flat against the rough grain of the wood. He refused to yield the sanctuary of this meal to tribal fragmentation. His Taurus polarity inverted his quiet contemplation into immovable, deadpan stubbornness. He dug his heels in, determined to enforce the communal roast ritual against the tide of their collective exhaustion.

Therefore, he stared directly at Kaio, refusing to blink or modulate his expression.

"If you're complaining and no one is laughing, you're complaining wrong," Elias stated.

The overlapping shouts faltered. The absurdity of the statement suspended the argument in the humid air of the hall, resetting their limbic baseline just enough to halt the cascade.

A quiet snort broke the silence. Elara leaned forward, picking up a pristine, empty bowl. She offered a grounded presence that effortlessly defused the remaining tension, ladling the contested stew with practiced grace. They sat together once more, sixteen mugs raised in the warm circle of firelight while the captured geode hums beneath the floorboards.
